A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSDPG research work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–N support reliable comparison despite repagination and revisions to the theory.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy reinforcement-learning and MuJoCo experiments in Section 6, with supervised-learning results and additional ablations in Appendices J–M.

after.justification: v3 retains the original reinforcement-learning, supervised-learning, and ablation results in Section 6 and Appendices J–M.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same DSDPG procedure: sampled return-gradient critics, a differentiable world model, MMD/MSMMD training, target truncation, and policy updates. The mathematical revisions do not establish a change to this procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same sinusoid-supervision problem, hidden-bonus point-mass task, and six MuJoCo environments with the same noise scenarios. Changing 'five' to 'six' in Section 6.2 corrects the description; Figure 3 already contains six environments in v1.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain TD3-Huber, MAGE/Huber Sobolev, IQN, MMD, and MSMMD. Although v3 removes MSMMD from Figure 3's caption, that comparator remains in the unchanged plotted results and legend.

E3.justification: The training horizons, UTD ratio of 10, distributional sample counts, noise settings, architectures, and Tables 1–2 parameters are retained. The appendix experiments also retain their evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Appendices J and M retain the limited-data and input-noise analyses, flow-world-model comparison, bias-correction ablation, and bandwidth, noise-scale, sample-count, and model-capacity studies. Section 6.2's correction from 'underestimation' to 'overestimation' describes the same existing ablation.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains five-seed medians and interquartile ranges; Figure 3 retains ten-seed medians and bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals. The appendix seed counts and statistical summaries are unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 6.2 corrects its performance summary from matching baselines across five tasks and outperforming them on three of five to six tasks and three of six. The underlying plotted scores, learning curves, appendix findings, and Table 3 runtimes remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a separate parameter-Lipschitz bound used in Proposition 1. Appendix D substantially revises Theorem 4's coupled-gradient assumptions and proof, corrects an unjustified equality, and removes v1's separate local-regularity Theorem 5. Appendix G specializes and consolidates the general affine contraction treatment and explicitly connects gradient liftings to the critic parametrization.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: joint return-gradient distribution modeling, DSDPG, contraction guarantees, the smoothness–discount trade-off, and improved robustness under stochastic conditions.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1's assertion that bounded network weights and Lipschitz activations ensure the derivative-coupling bound in Theorem 4, instead explicitly assuming compatible gradient liftings. This qualifies the theory's practical applicability; the empirical interpretations and computational limitations otherwise remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page footnote identifying an implementation repository for the JAX code. The existing pseudocode, architecture descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware information, and runtime reporting are retained.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning remain the same. The Goodfellow GAN reference changes from its earlier citation to publication details, and the Zhang reference receives bibliographic corrections; these do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted grammar, terminology, and cross-reference corrections and streamlines explanations around the revised proofs. The main section and appendix organization remains intact; the publication header changes and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 8 to page 7 and loses a redundant statistics annotation beneath its unchanged curves. All 18 figures and three tables remain, with limited caption edits and page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision by distinguishing parameter Lipschitzness, making gradient-coupling requirements explicit, and repairing Theorem 4's argument. It also corrects the six-task summary and adds implementation-access information. These gains support a limited overall improvement: the revised theory drops an alternative theorem and remains conditional on assumed liftings, while the empirical evidence is unchanged.
